reviews.text: Its a decent card battler. Graphics are fairly well done with some animations during battles. Cards are nice to look at. The presentation isn't that great but this is an indie title. Music and sound effects are below average. All in all though, if you enjoy deck building card battlers, it worth trying this out.

评分：2/5 评测：前期期待给的多高，后期失望就有多大。游戏的玩法很有新意，探索博物馆，和怪物进行卡牌对战，融合了解谜探索和卡牌对战两大玩法，以卡牌的形式来讲故事，很有意思。然而这个游戏后期的体验实在是相当的差，首先这个游戏不是肉鸽，因为死后重置的只有关卡中的怪，不会重置手牌，所以应该算是闯关解谜，这点是不错的。然而游戏却设计了一个非常迷惑的卡牌升级功能，把不同层级的怪物难度都成倍提高，导致玩家在每次进入新关卡时都必须死亡一次，把卡片全都升到下一级后才能打过下层的怪物。第一关的卡牌打不过第二关，升完第二关的卡牌还是打不过第三关，操作完全弥补不了成倍的数值差距，实属离谱。 碎片化太严重，缺点过于明显，不太推荐

The game has a lot of bugs and balancing to fix. There is no option for button settings, and they could only do with a mouse and not buttons. If you start a territory, the only way out is with a loss. If you press escape before losing, you can start the battle again. Some of the cards don't work properly as well as the balance. The enemy can become 3 to one and can always increase his blood plus more bonuses that you cannot. Each action is the same no matter what card you use. It's like a new age unlocks stronger and new cards, even the second age has protection, but the enemy is also increasing in every respect, giving too much. The story doesn't seem to be complete and the many limitations in the game make you grind a lot. Many things are not well thought out, they could have put a map. In the levels it is the same battle or not and main tasks nothing else. Battles get boring pretty quickly. Maybe if it passes the early access I would give it a chance but now it is bare bones. There are many more bugs.

Really enjoyed this until I got to the Russian Exhibit. I am not going to spoil anything but the deck I had made and the way I had played until that point became so woefully inadequate and completely unusable that I think the devs are trying to push players into adopting the new meta introduced in that area. . .I guess that is fine, but I sort of just wanted to do keep playing the way I had been and being pushed into something kind of put me off a bit. Honestly until that point though I loved everything. I liked the aesthetics, the game-play was straight forward, nothing was too difficult and everything remained pretty interesting, the environments were kind of great, it all really worked for me -loved the Hellenes particularly. The European Exhibit had a lot of tense encounters where I was coming back from single digit health which was always a great feeling. That last level though. . .when I died I didn't even bother to try again. I just uninstalled it. My only other complaint is that some cards can be upgraded and others can't and it isn't a restriction by their level so I wasn't really sure what the difference was. If I could have upgraded any cards I wanted to I would have been alright, but as it was. . .Not too bad. Good effort, most of the gameplay is solid and I feel confident this will eventually get to a place where it is 100% solid -but it isn't quite there yet.

For free game it is pretty good, puzzles, card customization, different synergies, lots of different enemies smooth graphics. You can turn your base card into powerful one over time, by careful selection and upgrading.

It pains me a bit but there is no way around giving this a "please leave it alone until the devs set things right": Two main reasons: - having cleared Aegypt and Roman period, i was led to go European middle ages next. Cool cool. But the big glowy door to Aegypt is pretty tempting, so i stepped in real quick. Aaaaand i'm hardlocked into completing Aegypt again. Game already auto-saved, door is closed without way back. So i had to go through all the walking simulator that already isn't theeeee strongest aspect of the game kinda, while also clearing away completely meaningless fights. It's cool that i can get cards from Aegypt that way if i want some, but ... ye ... => Open the door back OR put a "warp to lobby" option that can even remove all progress to be fair or whatevs OR have multiple autosave slots that cycle. Any of those will do it. - Secondly, the third boss, Arthur, is complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The fact that he cleanses ALL your buffs on every attack is completely unprecedented in the game. No warning whatsoever. Having built a completely OP Deck that revolves around multiple buff cards (+dmg per buff, heal on attack, 1x5 attack cards basically) surfing through the game kinda chill and then meeting a Boss that basically just tells me "no, we don't do that here" is .... lame as hell. Killed my desire to play the game from 100 to 0. I could probably have managed if he cleansed only one random buff per attack or had a conditional cleanse or something and it would have been an interesting encounter. But this fight was lost before the fight began, basically before i entered the museum even, and that is horrible game design. It's possible i'll reconsider this review in the future as the game does have potential. The museum theme is cool and the cards are okay. No complaints about the price either, obviously :P
I like it. Great art and the card synergize in fun ways. It gets repetitive pretty quickly like all these roguelike card games though.

I would give this game a rating in between yes and no, since I really like it but it still has some issues. The title screen says it is an early access version so I hope they will get fixed soon. The main mechanic is really fun and the game looks visually pleasing. However, there are still some problems, for example, I got locked in the canopic jars mission and could not progress or go back without resetting my progress. I did all four rooms and althoug I picked up all four jars, only one jar appeared in the main room. I did all the rooms again and two more jars appeared, but the fourth was nowhere to be found, so I was stuck. Going back to the entry resets your save point, which means I lost all three jars again that I managed to find, but at least I was able to do the rooms a third time and got all four jars this time. The reset did not give me the cat back though, so instead of giving it to the mummy I had to fight it. There are two other small issues I had that I hope will be fixed soon: I do not see any way to access the main lobby. I would like to upgrade my cards and such, but I see no way to do that since you cannot leave the current area except by dying and losing your progress. The other issue was that the game starts up in russian the first time you open it (instead of looking at your steam or device language) and therefore I had to use a translator app to find the language option. I will give a thumbs up, but I hope there will be some updates to better justify it.

Looks beautiful. Sometimes battles are interesting. Positives end there. Now onto the things that bother me. - [u][b]Nothing to do except fight![/b][/u] You have this huge open area, but barely anything to interact with. No random events so in-between battles are just long, boring walks to the next enemy to fight. No environmental interactions, even the few things you [i]can[/i] interact with only give you inspiration. Not even a popup of what the item is! (Though they do give you the info in your codex so at least there's that, but who's stopping to read?) - [u][b]Healing is.. something.[/b][/u] Instead of shielding, this game's version of damage nullification is.. nothing. You just get walloped in the face, but instead of loosing 5HP immediately, you get 5 wounds. If you don't treat your wounds by the end of the turn [i]then[/i] you will actually lose your 5HP. You start off with wound-heals, so you'll have to earn HP-heal cards via leveling up after each battle. (Or, you can forfeit getting any cards for healing 10HP straight up) That being said, one of the few times I think in combat, bc HP-heals can better your wounds, but your wounds will ONLY better your wounds. (3 wound + 5 bandage = 2 bandage [u]wasted[/u]) - No, seriously, the healing is something. [u][b]Enemies do not have a HP cap.[/b][/u] That means if they start with 30HP, they can heal ABOVE 30HP. Perhaps RNG is being cruel to me, but enemies can even have a heal on their first turn, so yeah, annoying. It forces you to tear your focus away from one enemy and genuinely watch all of them because you dont want that beetle to have 75HP by the time you turn to deal with it. - [u][b]Couple graphical bugs.[/b][/u] UI of the gift shop and the relic storage has the little info panel covering the left-most relic's popups, so Im thinking the game wasn't made to scale with your UI settings (I left mine on default). Steam's background recording function doesnt work with this lmao entire screen covered in the cursor. Some reflection issues (seen most prominently in the main lobby), and clipping issues with the camera and the environment (3rd last room from the Anubis boss room, there's scaffolding that gets cut off) Also, a pet peeve: No windowed mode, borderless windowed, etc. Just fullscreen. [u][b]TL;DR It's a free game, but I'd say even then it's a waste of your time until it's updated.[/b][/u] Read the other negative reviews; pretty sure those are real. The game does have potential though, and I might come back to it if there's an update, but as it stands, I think I'm okay for now.

The game was fun for 109 minutes lol, but for whatever reason, it no longer displays correctly. I have a dual monitor system, and even though the game should be playing on my main monitor, it always defaults to the secondary monitor. That monitor is arranged vertically, and the in game settings don't allow for a fix to that. I've tried using the properties in the steam interface as well as OS fixes. I also emailed the developers, but the email they provided returned to my inbox with an error. As of now, the game is totally broken for me, and I sadly won't be able to finish it. I'm really hoping these issues get resolved, and that the game will one day be finished.

This game has a LOT of promise. And I'm really excited to see what happens when it's finished cooking. But it's not finished yet. There is a lot of fighting, and if you go into a world you have to finish that world again. I'm fine with both of these things that have been listed as criticism. It's pokemon with museum exhibits, so I'm having fun with all that! My issue is in the Russia room. At some point i got petrified, and can no longer use the special move card. Also the clowns keep making me lose an action point, but I don't know why. So I'm stuck there. I keep dying and can't move forward. It's very frustrating. If it was just a massive jump in difficulty, fine, that would also be frustrating, but it's the loss of my ability to actually do anything that makes it a no for now. Also the fact that you can't save and when you close the game it goes from the last save point. That's another strike against it. But, I mean, I've played 12 hours of it already. I really want to play it when it's a little more polished!

I really wanted to like this as a poor man's version of Slay the Spire but it's just too repetitive. You're forced to do card battles against an insane number of the same boring enemies before you finally get to a more interesting encounter with a boss. Plus, it's got some pretty bad glitches that will do things like reset your progress on a floor if you walk too close to the place you entered that floor. The game also doesn't bother to explain what certain terms mean and the descriptions for some cards are poorly-written and confusing

"Museum Mystery: Deckbuilding Card Game" is, while it doesn't look like it right away, actually just a weak ripoff of games like Slay the Spire... a card battler where you go through a series of procgen fights, slinging out cards etc. The dungeon run theme of Slay the Spire was replaced with a badly translated Russian "Night at the Museum" theme that just... doesn't work at all. What do you do in the game? You play a worse version of Slay the Spire. The graphics in this game are passable, but could be better. And while it's vital for any game to have impressive visuals (gaming is a visual medium, after all), there's more to a game than just the graphics. To be worth a gamers time, the game must match top tier visuals with top tier gameplay, and that's not happening here. The developer chose not to do the job of a real game developer and create meaningful bespoke levels, narrative based gameplay progression and so on. Instead, they decided that "Procgen IS content!" and lazily tried to use procgen algorithms to create infinite, samey, repetitive, soulless levels, because that's a lot less work. As a result of this poor decision, the game gets tired and repetitive almost immediately. Developers must learn that procgen is a terrible substitute for creating real content. It should not be used as "ez-mode" for content creation, as the developer tried to do here. Now on to pricing and value for gamers. This is "free" enough (not every "free" game in the "free" section is truly free, there's usually some hidden price tag), at least you won't be expected to spend any more money after you download this, but just because something is free doesn't mean it's good, and the cost of a game is more than just financial, your time is valuable too. In terms of public reception, this failed. There's well over 130 million gamers on Steam. SteamDB showed the game peaked at less than 100 concurrent players, they couldn't even break three figures, and now there's basically nobody playing it. Even though it's free. This is a dismal public reception, but it's easy to see why gamers rejected it. It's important to note that, despite this being such a low quality product, there's a number of positive reviews that all appeared immediately after the game launched, from suspiciously inactive Steam accounts that have reviewed almost no other games apart from this. Take the review score of this game with a grain of salt. Given that this free title won't increase your game collector count, is it worth your time to add it to your library? I think you should give this one a miss. Although it's free, your time and storage are valuable resources, and the market is filled with superior options.

I want to be charged money for this game. I am invested in this game and this publisher. This game reminds me of the Nancy Drew games from herinteractive in the absolute best way possible. So much fun. A very unique take on a deck builder, and I am learning things in the process. No but really, where can I send money to help this game and this developer work long term.

I just spent a weekend playing this game. I saw some of the negative reviews, but i cant say any of those things really bothered me. I was mostly focused on unlocking new cards and figuring out a way to break the game with a strong combo, while enjoying the atmosphere. By the last chapter, I ended up one-shoting almost everything except the final boss. Overall, I found it enjoyable.
It's not the best game of its kind, but there are some nice ideas and its much longer than I expected from a free game (I assume I finished about 75% of the main game).
